title: Titan Notes: Segment Margins Hide the Real Jewellery Story
scenario: You're a junior analyst on the Mumbai desk covering Titan Company Limited. The FY24 consolidated results look solid — but your senior just asked: 'What's really driving profit? Are all segments pulling their weight, or is one carrying the other?' Time to hit the segment note.
instructions: Read Titan's FY24 financial statement and notes. Hover tooltips on key line items. Answer questions about revenue breakdown, segment margins, and what the consolidated numbers hide.
learning_objective: Compute segment margins to un-blend a multi-business company and identify which divisions drive or drag consolidated profit.
hints: Look at the segment note — you'll find revenue and profit broken out by Jewellery, Watches, and Eyewear. Profit ÷ Revenue for each.
Jewellery is the big beast — it's driving the scale. But check whether it's also driving the *margin*. Compare it to Watches and Eyewear margins.
Segment Margin = (Segment Profit ÷ Segment Revenue) × 100. Compute for all three, then ask: which segment is most profitable per rupee, and which is the profit driver?

interactive_highlights.tooltip: Consolidated operating revenue — the blend of all three segments (Jewellery, Watches, Eyewear) plus corporate adjustments. See Note 48 to un-blend by segment and compute each margin.
Includes distribution, marketing, administrative, and store-operating costs across all segments. Significant allocation judgment — read the segment note to understand which segment bears which share.
Jewellery profit of ₹3,294 cr on ₹18,240 cr revenue = 18.1% margin — check this against Watches and Eyewear to see if Jewellery is truly the profit driver or just the volume driver.
Watches profit of ₹1,476 cr on ₹5,680 cr revenue = 26.0% margin — a premium margin, suggesting Watches is a higher-quality business per rupee than the blended company average implies.

Consolidated EBIT of ₹7,867 cr is the sum of segment profits (less corporate allocations). The segments note breaks this down — critical for understanding which business is funding which, and whether any segment is a loss-making drag.

tasks.question: What is the Watches segment margin (Profit ÷ Revenue, %) for FY24?
tasks.explanation: (1476 ÷ 5680) × 100 = 25.96% ≈ 26.0%. Watches is a premium, high-margin segment — much higher than the consolidated company average of ~21.6%, and higher than Jewellery's ~18.1%. This is a classic un-blending insight: the consolidated margin hides the fact that Watches is a far superior business on its own.

tasks.question: Which segment is the profit driver — highest absolute profit in FY24?
tasks.explanation: Jewellery generated ₹3,294 cr profit, vs Watches ₹1,476 cr and Eyewear ₹810 cr. Jewellery is the largest profit contributor in absolute terms, even though its margin (18.1%) is lower than Watches (26.0%). Volume dominates; Watches is higher-quality but smaller.

tasks.question: Revenue from operations grew ₹4,360 cr YoY. Estimate what % of that incremental revenue came from Jewellery.
tasks.explanation: Jewellery revenue growth = 18240 - 15480 = ₹2,760 cr. Total revenue growth = 28540 - 24180 = ₹4,360 cr. Jewellery's share = (2760 ÷ 4360) × 100 = 63.3%. Jewellery is the growth engine — Watches and Eyewear contribute growth, but Jewellery is driving the consolidated growth story.

tasks.question: The consolidated profit margin (Profit ÷ Revenue) for FY24 is approximately which percentage?
tasks.explanation: (6157 ÷ 28540) × 100 = 21.58% ≈ 21.6%. This blended margin is useful as a headline, but it masks the fact that Watches (26.0%) is significantly more profitable than the average, while Jewellery (18.1%) and Eyewear (25.9%) sit around or above it. Segment margins tell the real story.

tasks.question: Based on the segment data, which statement is true: (A) Jewellery is more profitable per rupee than Watches, (B) Watches is more profitable per rupee than Jewellery, or (C) both segments have identical margin?
tasks.explanation: Watches margin (26.0%) > Jewellery margin (18.1%), so (B) is correct. This is the core un-blending insight: Jewellery dominates in volume and absolute profit, but Watches is a fundamentally higher-quality, higher-margin business. A consolidated-only reader would miss this, and might over-weight Jewellery's strategic importance when Watches is actually the margin anchor.
